# 12-Week General Strength Programme
## Client Profile: 42M, Desk Worker, Post-Disc Herniation (L4-L5, Asymptomatic)

---

## Programme Overview

This 12-week plan prioritises spinal stability and neutral-spine strength while building general fitness. The programme avoids loaded spinal flexion and heavy axial loading through the lumbar spine. Sessions are structured around compound movements performed with strict form, progressing load conservatively.

**Structure:** 4 sessions per week across 3 phases
- **Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4):** Movement quality, stability foundation, moderate intensity
- **Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8):** Strength development, load progression, movement complexity
- **Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12):** Strength consolidation, power introduction, sport-specific conditioning

---

## Key Principles

1. **Neutral spine maintained** throughout all exercises; no loaded spinal flexion (no heavy deadlifts from floor, no loaded sit-ups, no heavy bent-over rows)
2. **Anti-rotation and anti-extension work** to build core stability
3. **Bilateral and unilateral lower-body work** to address asymmetries from desk work
4. **Upper-body pulling emphasis** to counteract anterior chain dominance
5. **Progressive overload** via reps, load, or density—never at the expense of form
6. **Warm-up and mobility** integrated into every session

---

## Session Structure (All 4 Sessions)

**Warm-up (8–10 minutes)**
- 3 min easy cardio (rowing, bike, or walk)
- Mobility: cat-cow, quadruped thoracic rotation, 90/90 hip stretch, glute bridges (2×8)
- Movement prep: bodyweight squats, push-ups, bird dogs (2×6 each side)

**Main Work (40–45 minutes)**
- A1/A2 superset or A/B pairing (strength focus)
- B1/B2 superset (secondary strength or hypertrophy)
- C: Core/stability work
- D: Conditioning or accessory (as prescribed)

**Cool-down (5 minutes)**
- Light stretching: hip flexor, hamstring, chest, lat

---

## PHASE 1: Foundation & Stability (Weeks 1–4)

### Goals
- Establish movement quality and neutral-spine awareness
- Build core stability and glute activation
- Assess baseline strength and movement competency
- Prepare tissues for progressive loading

### Session A: Lower Body & Core (Monday)

**Warm-up** (as above)

**A1. Goblet Squat**
- 4 sets × 8 reps
- 12 kg kettlebell, 2 min rest
- *Cue:* Chest up, knees tracking over toes, neutral spine, full depth if pain-free

**A2. Dead Bug (Alternating Arm/Leg)**
- 4 sets × 6 each side
- Bodyweight, 60 sec rest
- *Cue:* Lower back flat to floor, move slowly, exhale on extension

**B1. Split Squat (Rear Foot Elevated)**
- 3 sets × 8 each leg
- Bodyweight, 90 sec rest
- *Cue:* Front knee over ankle, upright torso, rear knee lightly touches floor

**B2. Pallof Press (Half-Kneeling)**
- 3 sets × 8 each side
- 8 kg cable, 60 sec rest
- *Cue:* Resist rotation, brace core, press straight ahead

**C. Glute Bridge Hold + Marching**
- 3 sets × 20 sec hold + 10 marches
- Bodyweight, 60 sec rest
- *Cue:* Squeeze glutes hard, neutral spine, hips level

---

### Session B: Upper Body Push & Pull (Tuesday)

**Warm-up** (as above)

**A1. Dumbbell Bench Press**
- 4 sets × 8 reps
- 16 kg dumbbells, 2 min rest
- *Cue:* Shoulder blades retracted, elbows at 45°, controlled descent

**A2. Inverted Row (Assisted if Needed)**
- 4 sets × 8 reps
- Barbell at chest height or TRX, 2 min rest
- *Cue:* Chest to bar, elbows tucked, neutral spine, full retraction

**B1. Landmine Press (Single-Arm)**
- 3 sets × 8 each side
- 8 kg plate, 90 sec rest
- *Cue:* Core braced, no spinal extension, press at 45° angle

**B2. Lat Pulldown (Neutral Grip)**
- 3 sets × 10 reps
- 40 kg, 90 sec rest
- *Cue:* Elbows down and back, chest up, no spinal flexion

**C. Prone Shoulder Taps**
- 3 sets × 10 each side
- Plank position, 60 sec rest
- *Cue:* Hips level, minimal rotation, controlled tap

---

### Session C: Lower Body & Stability (Thursday)

**Warm-up** (as above)

**A1. Trap Bar Deadlift (Light)**
- 4 sets × 6 reps
- 40 kg (bar only or light load), 2 min rest
- *Cue:* Neutral spine, chest up, drive through heels, no lumbar rounding

**A2. Bird Dog (Contralateral)**
- 4 sets × 6 each side
- Bodyweight, 60 sec rest
- *Cue:* Extend opposite arm and leg, no rotation, exhale on extension

**B1. Bulgarian Split Squat**
- 3 sets × 8 each leg
- Bodyweight, 90 sec rest
- *Cue:* Rear foot elevated, front knee over ankle, upright torso

**B2. Single-Leg Glute Bridge**
- 3 sets × 8 each leg
- Bodyweight, 60 sec rest
- *Cue:* Squeeze glutes, hips level, neutral spine

**C. Suitcase Carry**
- 3 sets × 30 m each side
- 12 kg dumbbell, walk slowly
- *Cue:* Resist lateral flexion, shoulders level, core braced

---

### Session D: Upper Body & Conditioning (Friday)

**Warm-up** (as above)

**A1. Dumbbell Rows (Alternating)**
- 4 sets × 8 each side
- 16 kg dumbbells, 2 min rest
- *Cue:* Neutral spine, elbow tucked, full retraction, no rotation

**A2. Push-Up (Incline or Flat)**
- 4 sets × 8 reps
- Incline bench or floor, 2 min rest
- *Cue:* Elbows at 45°, neutral spine, full range, controlled descent

**B1. Face Pull**
- 3 sets × 12 reps
- 12 kg cable, 90 sec rest
- *Cue:* Elbows high, external rotation, retract shoulder blades

**B2. Chest-Supported Row (Machine or Incline Bench)**
- 3 sets × 10 reps
- 30 kg machine, 90 sec rest
- *Cue:* Chest supported, elbows tucked, full retraction

**C. Conditioning: Rowing Machine**
- 4 × 2 min at moderate intensity, 1 min rest
- *Cue:* Legs, core, arms sequence; maintain neutral spine

---

## PHASE 2: Strength Development (Weeks 5–8)

### Goals
- Increase load on primary lifts while maintaining form
- Introduce more complex movement patterns
- Build work capacity and conditioning
- Develop unilateral strength asymmetries

### Progression from Phase 1
- Increase loads by 10–15% where possible
- Add reps or sets to secondary exercises
- Introduce tempo variation and pauses
- Reduce rest periods slightly to increase density

---

### Session A: Lower Body & Core (Monday)

**Warm-up** (as above)

**A1. Trap Bar Deadlift**
- 5 sets × 5 reps
- 60 kg (progressive: +5 kg per week if form holds), 2.5 min rest
- *Cue:* Neutral spine, explosive drive, full hip extension, no lumbar extension

**A2. Pallof Press (Standing)**
- 4 sets × 8 each side
- 12 kg cable, 90 sec rest
- *Cue:* Resist rotation, brace hard, press with control

**B1. Reverse Sled Push (or Leg Press)**
- 3 sets × 8 reps
- 80 kg sled (or 100 kg leg press), 2 min rest
- *Cue:* Neutral spine, full range, controlled descent

**B2. Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift (Light Dumbbell)**
- 3 sets × 8 each leg
- 8 kg dumbbell, 90 sec rest
- *Cue:* Neutral spine, hip hinge, balance, light load for control

**C. Plank Variations (Alternating)**
- Week 5–6: Standard plank 3 × 45 sec
- Week 7–8: Plank with shoulder taps 3 × 10 each side
- 60 sec rest between sets

---

### Session B: Upper Body Push & Pull (Tuesday)

**Warm-up** (as above)

**A1. Dumbbell Bench Press**
- 5 sets × 5 reps
- 18 kg dumbbells (progressive), 2.5 min rest
- *Cue:* Shoulder blades retracted, elbows at 45°, full range, explosive concentric

**A2. Barbell Bent-Over Row (Slight Incline, Neutral Spine)**
- 5 sets × 5 reps
- 30 kg (progressive: +2.5 kg per week), 2.5 min rest
- *Cue:* Slight forward lean (not heavy flexion), chest up, elbows tucked, full retraction

**B1. Landmine Press (Single-Arm)**
- 3 sets × 8 each side
- 10 kg plate, 90 sec rest
- *Cue:* Core braced, no spinal extension, stable base

**B2. Lat Pulldown (Neutral Grip)**
- 3 sets × 10 reps
- 50 kg (progressive), 90 sec rest
- *Cue:* Elbows down and back, no spinal flexion, full retraction

**C. Conditioning: Assault Bike**
- 5 × 1 min hard, 1 min easy
- Moderate resistance, 60 sec rest between efforts

---

### Session C: Lower Body & Stability (Thursday)

**Warm-up** (as above)

**A1. Goblet Squat (Heavier)**
- 4 sets × 6 reps
- 16 kg kettlebell, 2 min rest
- *Cue:* Chest up, full depth, neutral spine, explosive drive

**A2. Dead Bug (Weighted)**
- 4 sets × 6 each side
- 2 kg plate on chest, 90 sec rest
- *Cue:* Lower back flat, slow and controlled, exhale on extension

**B1. Bulgarian Split Squat (Dumbbell)**
- 3 sets × 8 each leg
- 12 kg dumbbells, 2 min rest
- *Cue:* Front knee over ankle, upright torso, full range

**B2. Copenhagen Adductor Squeeze**
- 3 sets × 12 reps
- Slider or pillow between knees, 60 sec rest
- *Cue:* Squeeze hard, neutral spine, controlled release

**C. Farmer's Carry (Heavy)**
- 3 sets × 40 m each side
- 16 kg dumbbells, walk with purpose
- *Cue:* Shoulders level, core braced, upright posture

---

### Session D: Upper Body & Conditioning (Friday)

**Warm-up** (as above)

**A1. Dumbbell Rows (Alternating, Heavier)**
- 5 sets × 5 each side
- 18 kg dumbbells, 2 min rest
- *Cue:* Neutral spine, explosive pull, full retraction, no rotation

**A2. Push-Up (Tempo)**
- 4 sets × 8 reps
- 3 sec descent, 1 sec pause, explosive ascent, 2 min rest
- *Cue:* Elbows at 45°, neutral spine, full range

**B1. Face Pull (Higher Reps)**
- 3 sets × 15 reps
- 14 kg cable, 90 sec rest
- *Cue:* Elbows high, external rotation, retract shoulder blades

**B2. Chest-Supported Row (Heavier)**
- 3 sets × 8 reps
- 40 kg machine, 2 min rest
- *Cue:* Chest supported, elbows tucked, explosive pull

**C. Conditioning: Row + Bike Finisher**
- 3 rounds: 500 m row + 30 sec bike sprint, 2 min rest
- Moderate-to-hard intensity

---

## PHASE 3: Strength Consolidation & Power (Weeks 9–12)

### Goals
- Consolidate strength gains with heavier loads
- Introduce power and speed-strength work
- Build sport-specific conditioning
- Maintain movement quality under fatigue

### Progression from Phase 2
- Increase loads by 5–10% on primary lifts
- Reduce reps on strength work (3–5 range)
- Add explosive/power variations
- Increase conditioning volume and intensity

---

### Session A: Lower Body & Core (Monday)

**Warm-up** (as above, add 2 × 3 jump squats for power prep)

**A1. Trap Bar Deadlift (Heavy)**
- 5 sets × 3 reps
- 70 kg (progressive: +2.5 kg per week), 3 min rest
- *Cue:* Explosive drive, full hip extension, neutral spine throughout

**A2. Pallof Press (Heavy)**
- 4 sets × 6 each side
- 16 kg cable, 2 min rest
- *Cue:* Resist rotation hard, brace core, press with control

**B1. Reverse Sled Push (Heavy)**
- 3 sets × 6 reps
- 100 kg sled, 2.5 min rest
- *Cue:* Explosive drive, neutral spine, full range

**B2. Single-Leg Deadlift (Dumbbell)**
- 3 sets × 6 each leg
- 10 kg dumbbell, 2 min rest
- *Cue:* Neutral spine, hip hinge, balance, controlled tempo

**C. Plank Variations (Advanced)**
- Week 9–10: Plank with alternating leg lifts 3 × 8 each leg
- Week 11–12: Plank with alternating arm + leg lifts 3 × 6 each side
- 90 sec rest between sets

## Nutrition & Recovery Guidance

### Nutrition
- **Protein:** 1.6–2.0 g per kg bodyweight daily (spread across 4–5 meals)
- **Carbohydrates:** 4–6 g per kg bodyweight daily, timed around training
- **Fats:** 0.8–1.2 g per kg bodyweight daily
- **Hydration:** 3–4 L water daily; more on training days
- **Pre-workout (1–2 hours before):** Light carbs + protein (e.g., banana + Greek yogurt)
- **Post-workout (within 30–60 min):** Protein + carbs (e.g., whey shake + rice cakes)

### Recovery
- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours nightly; prioritise consistency
- **Mobility:** 10 min daily (cat-cow, 90/90 hip stretch, thoracic rotation, glute bridges)
- **Foam rolling:** 5 min on quads, hamstrings, glutes, lats (avoid rolling directly on spine)
- **Deload week:** Every 4 weeks, reduce volume by 40–50% and load by 20–30%
- **Monitoring:** Track RPE (Rate of Perceived Exertion) on main lifts; aim for 7–8/10 on heavy days

---

## Deload Weeks (Weeks 4, 8, 12)

Reduce volume and load to allow recovery and prevent overuse injury.

**Deload Structure:**
- Same exercises, same 4 sessions per week
- Reduce load by 20–30%
- Reduce sets by 1–2 per exercise
- Increase rest periods by 30 sec
- Focus on movement quality and mobility
- Example: If Week 4 Trap Bar Deadlift is 5 × 5 @ 60 kg, deload is 3 × 5 @ 45 kg

---

## Monitoring & Adjustments

### Red Flags (Stop or Modify)
- Any sharp or shooting pain in lower back
- Numbness or tingling in legs
- Loss of form under fatigue
- Persistent soreness beyond 48 hours

### Progression Criteria
- Complete all prescribed reps with good form
- RPE ≤ 8/10 on final set
- No pain or discomfort during or after session
- If criteria met, increase load by 2.5–5 kg next week

### Regression Options
- Reduce load by 10–15%
- Reduce reps by 2–3
- Increase rest periods by 30–60 sec
- Substitute with easier variation (e.g., incline push-up instead of flat)

- Improve recovery between training sessions

## Cardio Principles for Disc Herniation Recovery

### Safety Considerations
1. **Avoid high-impact activities** that create spinal compression or jarring (running on hard surfaces, jumping rope)
2. **Maintain neutral spine** during all cardio (upright posture on bike/rower, no excessive forward lean)
3. **Gradual progression** in duration and intensity; build aerobic base before high-intensity work
4. **Low-impact modalities** prioritised: rowing, cycling, swimming, elliptical, assault bike
5. **Monitor for pain or discomfort** during and after sessions; stop immediately if sharp pain occurs

### Benefits of Cardio for This Client
- Improves cardiovascular fitness and work capacity
- Enhances recovery between strength sessions (active recovery)
- Supports metabolic health and body composition
- Reduces systemic inflammation (complements anti-inflammatory diet)
- Improves mood and mental health (desk worker benefit)
- Builds aerobic base for conditioning work in Phase 3

## Cardio Modality Selection

### Recommended Modalities (Ranked by Safety & Effectiveness)

| Modality | Safety | Effectiveness | Notes |
|----------|--------|----------------|-------|
| **Rowing Machine** | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | Full-body, low-impact, neutral spine, excellent for core stability |

### Avoid

## Cardio Form Cues by Modality

### Rowing Machine (Preferred for Spinal Safety)

**Setup:**
- Seat height: mid-shin when legs extended
- Footplate straps: snug but not tight
- Monitor distance: arm's length away

**Movement Sequence (Legs → Core → Arms):**
1. **Catch position:** Shins vertical, arms extended, shoulders relaxed, neutral spine
2. **Drive:** Push with legs first (70% of power), maintaining neutral spine
3. **Finish:** As legs extend, engage core and pull arms to chest
4. **Recovery:** Extend arms, hinge at hips (slight forward lean, ~20°), bend knees to return to catch

**Cues:**
- "Legs first, then core, then arms"
- "Maintain upright torso; no excessive spinal flexion"
- "Smooth, rhythmic strokes; avoid jerky movements"
- "Breathe out on drive, in on recovery"
- **Avoid:** Rounding lower back, pulling with arms first, excessive forward lean

---

### Stationary Bike (Upright)

**Setup:**
- Seat height: knee slightly bent (15–20°) at bottom of pedal stroke
- Seat position: directly above pedal axle (neutral)
- Handlebar height: level with seat or slightly higher (avoid excessive forward lean)

**Movement:**
- Pedal in smooth, circular motion
- Cadence: 80–90 RPM (steady state), 90–100 RPM (intervals)
- Engage core; avoid rocking side-to-side

**Cues:**
- "Upright posture; shoulders relaxed"
- "Smooth, circular pedal stroke"
- "Steady cadence; avoid jerky movements"
- "Breathe rhythmically; exhale on harder efforts"
- **Avoid:** Excessive forward lean, white-knuckling handlebars, standing (unless specified)

---

### Assault/Air Bike

**Setup:**
- Seat height: knee slightly bent at bottom of pedal stroke
- Seat position: neutral, directly above pedal axle
- Handlebar height: comfortable, allowing upright posture

**Movement:**
- Pedal and push/pull handlebars simultaneously
- Cadence: 80–100 RPM (varies with resistance)
- Full-body engagement: legs, core, arms, shoulders

**Cues:**
- "Upright posture; core engaged"
- "Smooth, powerful pedal stroke"
- "Push and pull handlebars with intention"
- "Breathe rhythmically; exhale on hard efforts"
- **Avoid:** Excessive forward lean, jerky movements, holding breath

---

### Swimming (If Available)

**Modalities:**
- **Freestyle (Front Crawl):** Most efficient, low-impact
- **Backstroke:** Excellent for posterior chain; zero spinal flexion
- **Breaststroke:** Gentler; avoid excessive spinal extension
- **Kickboard work:** Isolate legs; build lower-body endurance

**Cues:**
- "Maintain neutral spine; avoid excessive arching or flexion"
- "Smooth, controlled strokes"
- "Bilateral breathing (every 3 strokes) for balance"
- "Engage core throughout"
- **Avoid:** Excessive spinal extension (especially backstroke), jerky movements

## Monitoring & Adjustments for Cardio

### Red Flags (Stop or Modify)
- Sharp or shooting pain in lower back during or after cardio
- Numbness or tingling in legs
- Excessive fatigue affecting strength sessions
- Elevated resting heart rate (>10 bpm above baseline)
- Persistent soreness or joint pain

### Regression Options
- **Reduce intensity:** Lower RPE by 1–2 points
- **Reduce duration:** Shorten session by 5–10 minutes
- **Reduce frequency:** Drop to 1 cardio session per week temporarily
- **Change modality:** Switch to lower-impact option (e.g., bike instead of rowing)
- **Increase recovery:** Add extra rest day between cardio and strength

### Progression Criteria
- Complete all prescribed intervals with good form
- RPE matches target (e.g., 8–9/10 on hard efforts)
- No pain or discomfort during or after session
- Resting heart rate stable or improving
- Strength sessions unaffected by cardio fatigue

# Safe Core & Abs Work for Post-Disc Herniation Client

---

## Core Training Principles for Disc Herniation Recovery

### Key Constraints
1. **No loaded spinal flexion** (no heavy sit-ups, crunches, weighted cable crunches)
2. **No repetitive spinal flexion** (even bodyweight crunches are risky; disc herniation can be aggravated by repeated flexion)
3. **No excessive spinal extension** (avoid hyperextension exercises like back extensions)
4. **Prioritise anti-rotation and anti-lateral flexion** (these movements stabilise the spine and protect the disc)
5. **Emphasise isometric holds and controlled movements** (build stability, not just strength)

### Why This Matters
The L4-L5 disc herniation occurred likely due to repeated or heavy spinal flexion (common in desk workers who slouch). Even though it's asymptomatic now, the disc is still healing and remodelling. Loaded or repetitive flexion can re-aggravate it. Instead, we build a **stable, resilient core** that protects the spine during all activities.

---

## Safe Core & Abs Exercises by Category

### Category 1: Anti-Rotation Work (Primary Focus)

These exercises teach the core to resist rotation, which is essential for spinal stability and functional strength.

#### **1. Pallof Press (Half-Kneeling)**
- **Setup:** Half-kneeling position (one knee down, one foot forward), cable machine at chest height
- **Movement:** Brace core, press cable straight ahead, resist rotation
- **Sets/Reps:** 3–4 × 8–12 each side
- **Progression:** Increase load, add pause at end, perform standing
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to resist rotation; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Brace hard, press straight, don't let your torso twist"

#### **2. Pallof Press (Standing)**
- **Setup:** Standing perpendicular to cable machine, feet shoulder-width apart, cable at chest height
- **Movement:** Brace core, press cable straight ahead, resist rotation
- **Sets/Reps:** 3–4 × 8–12 each side
- **Progression:** Increase load, add step forward while pressing, add rotation (press, rotate, return)
- **Why Safe:** Standing variation; more functional; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Shoulders level, core braced, press with control"

#### **3. Landmine Rotation (Anti-Rotation Hold)**
- **Setup:** Landmine at chest height, feet shoulder-width apart, hold end of bar at chest
- **Movement:** Brace core, hold bar at chest without rotating; resist urge to twist
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 30–45 sec each side
- **Progression:** Increase duration, add light load, perform single-leg
- **Why Safe:** Isometric anti-rotation; builds stability
- **Cue:** "Shoulders square, core tight, resist rotation"

#### **4. Suitcase Carry (Unilateral Load)**
- **Setup:** Standing, holding dumbbell or kettlebell in one hand at side
- **Movement:** Walk slowly, resisting lateral flexion; keep shoulders level
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 30–40 m each side
- **Progression:** Increase load, increase distance, add tempo variation
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to resist lateral flexion; functional movement
- **Cue:** "Shoulders level, core braced, walk tall"

#### **5. Offset Dumbbell Carry (Unilateral Load)**
- **Setup:** Standing, holding dumbbell in one hand at shoulder height (like a goblet squat position)
- **Movement:** Walk slowly, resisting lateral flexion and rotation
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 30–40 m each side
- **Progression:** Increase load, increase distance, add tempo variation
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to resist multiple planes of movement
- **Cue:** "Shoulders level, core braced, walk tall"

#### **6. Chop (Cable or Landmine)**
- **Setup:** Standing perpendicular to cable machine (or landmine), feet shoulder-width apart, cable at shoulder height
- **Movement:** Rotate torso, bringing cable diagonally across body (like chopping wood), return with control
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 10–12 each side
- **Progression:** Increase load, add pause at end, perform half-kneeling
- **Why Safe:** Controlled rotation; teaches core to generate and control rotational force
- **Cue:** "Rotate from core, not arms; control the return"

#### **7. Reverse Chop (Cable or Landmine)**
- **Setup:** Standing perpendicular to cable machine, feet shoulder-width apart, cable at hip height
- **Movement:** Rotate torso, bringing cable diagonally up and across body (reverse of chop), return with control
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 10–12 each side
- **Progression:** Increase load, add pause at end, perform half-kneeling
- **Why Safe:** Controlled rotation; teaches core to resist and generate rotational force
- **Cue:** "Rotate from core, control the movement"

---

### Category 2: Anti-Extension Work (Secondary Focus)

These exercises teach the core to resist spinal extension, preventing hyperextension and protecting the disc.

#### **1. Dead Bug (Alternating Arm/Leg)**
- **Setup:** Lying on back, arms extended toward ceiling, knees bent at 90°, lower back flat to floor
- **Movement:** Extend opposite arm and leg slowly, maintaining lower back contact with floor, return
- **Sets/Reps:** 3–4 × 8–12 each side
- **Progression:** Add weight (light dumbbell on chest), increase tempo, perform with arms/legs extended
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to stabilise spine during limb movement; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Lower back stays flat, move slowly, exhale on extension"

#### **2. Bird Dog (Contralateral)**
- **Setup:** Quadruped position (hands and knees), neutral spine, core engaged
- **Movement:** Extend opposite arm and leg slowly, maintaining neutral spine, return
- **Sets/Reps:** 3–4 × 8–12 each side
- **Progression:** Add pause at end, increase tempo, perform with eyes closed (balance challenge)
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to stabilise during limb extension; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Extend with control, no rotation, exhale on extension"

#### **3. Prone Shoulder Taps (Plank Variation)**
- **Setup:** Plank position, hands under shoulders, neutral spine, core engaged
- **Movement:** Tap opposite shoulder with hand, maintaining level hips, return
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 10–12 each side
- **Progression:** Increase tempo, add pause, perform on unstable surface (BOSU ball)
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to stabilise during upper-body movement; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Hips level, minimal rotation, controlled tap"

#### **4. Plank Hold (Standard)**
- **Setup:** Forearm plank position, elbows under shoulders, neutral spine, core engaged
- **Movement:** Hold position, maintaining neutral spine and level hips
- **Sets/Reps:** 3–4 × 30–60 sec
- **Progression:** Increase duration, add shoulder taps, add leg lifts, perform on unstable surface
- **Why Safe:** Isometric core stability; zero spinal flexion or extension
- **Cue:** "Neutral spine, hips level, breathe steadily"

#### **5. Plank with Alternating Leg Lifts**
- **Setup:** Forearm plank position, neutral spine, core engaged
- **Movement:** Lift one leg slightly off ground, lower, repeat on other side
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 8–10 each leg
- **Progression:** Increase height of lift, add pause, increase tempo
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to stabilise during limb movement; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Hips level, core braced, lift with control"

#### **6. Plank with Alternating Arm + Leg Lifts**
- **Setup:** Forearm plank position, neutral spine, core engaged
- **Movement:** Extend opposite arm and leg simultaneously, return
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 6–8 each side
- **Progression:** Increase duration, add pause, increase tempo
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to stabilise during multi-planar movement; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Extend with control, hips level, exhale on extension"

#### **7. Glute Bridge Hold**
- **Setup:** Lying on back, knees bent, feet flat, arms at sides
- **Movement:** Drive through heels, lift hips to create straight line from knees to shoulders, hold
- **Sets/Reps:** 3–4 × 30–45 sec
- **Progression:** Increase duration, add marching (lift one foot), perform single-leg
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core and glutes to stabilise spine; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Squeeze glutes hard, hips level, neutral spine"

#### **8. Glute Bridge with Marching**
- **Setup:** Glute bridge hold position
- **Movement:** Lift one foot slightly off ground, lower, repeat on other side
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 10–12 each leg
- **Progression:** Increase tempo, add pause, increase duration
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to stabilise during limb movement; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Squeeze glutes, hips level, march with control"

#### **9. Single-Leg Glute Bridge**
- **Setup:** Lying on back, one knee bent (foot flat), other leg extended
- **Movement:** Drive through bent leg, lift hips, hold
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 8–12 each leg
- **Progression:** Increase duration, add pause, add upper-body movement
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to stabilise during unilateral movement; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Squeeze glutes, hips level, neutral spine"

### Category 3: Anti-Lateral Flexion Work (Secondary Focus)

These exercises teach the core to resist lateral bending, protecting the disc from side-to-side stress.

#### **1. Side Plank (Standard)**
- **Setup:** Lying on side, forearm under shoulder, neutral spine, core engaged
- **Movement:** Lift hips off ground, creating straight line from head to feet, hold
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 20–45 sec each side
- **Progression:** Increase duration, add hip dips, add top-leg lifts, perform on unstable surface
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to resist lateral flexion; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Hips level, core braced, neutral spine"

#### **2. Side Plank with Hip Dips**
- **Setup:** Side plank position
- **Movement:** Lower hips toward ground, raise back to level, repeat
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 10–12 each side
- **Progression:** Increase reps, add pause at bottom, increase tempo
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to resist and control lateral flexion; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Control the dip, hips level, core braced"

#### **3. Side Plank with Top-Leg Lift**
- **Setup:** Side plank position
- **Movement:** Lift top leg, lower, repeat
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 10–12 each side
- **Progression:** Increase reps, add pause, increase tempo
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to stabilise during lateral movement; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Hips level, lift with control, core braced"

#### **4. Copenhagen Adductor Squeeze (Lying)**
- **Setup:** Lying on side, bottom leg extended, top leg bent with knee on slider or pillow
- **Movement:** Squeeze top leg down toward bottom leg, hold, release
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 12–15 reps each side
- **Progression:** Increase reps, add pause, increase tempo
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core and adductors to stabilise; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Squeeze hard, control the release"

#### **5. Landmine Lateral Press (Half-Kneeling)**
- **Setup:** Half-kneeling position perpendicular to landmine, landmine at shoulder height
- **Movement:** Press landmine away laterally, resist lateral flexion, return
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 8–10 each side
- **Progression:** Increase load, add pause, perform standing
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to resist lateral flexion under load; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Core braced, press with control, resist lateral bend"

### Category 4: Isometric Core Holds (Foundational)

These exercises build core endurance and stability without dynamic movement.

#### **1. Dead Bug Hold (Isometric)**
- **Setup:** Lying on back, arms extended toward ceiling, knees bent at 90°, lower back flat
- **Movement:** Hold position, maintaining lower back contact with floor
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 30–45 sec
- **Progression:** Increase duration, extend arms/legs, add light weight
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to stabilise; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Lower back stays flat, breathe steadily"

#### **2. Bird Dog Hold (Isometric)**
- **Setup:** Quadruped position, opposite arm and leg extended, neutral spine
- **Movement:** Hold position, maintaining neutral spine
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 20–30 sec each side
- **Progression:** Increase duration, add balance challenge
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to stabilise; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Neutral spine, breathe steadily, hold with control"

#### **3. Hollow Body Hold**
- **Setup:** Lying on back, arms extended overhead, legs extended, lower back flat to floor
- **Movement:** Engage core, press lower back into floor, hold
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 × 20–30 sec
- **Progression:** Increase duration, add small rocking motion, perform on incline
- **Why Safe:** Teaches core to stabilise in extended position; zero spinal flexion
- **Cue:** "Lower back flat, core braced, breathe steadily"

## Overview

Week 12 will be restructured as a **1RM testing week** across the primary lifts. This allows your client to assess strength gains over the 12-week programme and provides a psychological boost from testing maximal strength. The week is strategically designed to:

1. **Prioritise recovery** leading into testing days
2. **Test one primary lift per session** (Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday)
3. **Maintain spinal safety** throughout the testing process
4. **Reduce volume** on non-testing days to preserve energy
5. **Provide adequate rest** between attempts

## Week 12 Structure: 1RM Testing Week

### Monday: Trap Bar Deadlift 1RM Test

**Warm-up (15 minutes)**
- 3 min easy rowing (RPE 3–4/10)

- 3 reps @ 50% estimated 1RM
- 2 reps @ 70% estimated 1RM
- 1 rep @ 85% estimated 1RM

**Attempt 1: Conservative Opening (85% of Estimated 1RM)**
- Load: 60 kg (based on Week 11 working weight of 70 kg × 3 reps)

- **Goal:** Establish new 1RM

## 1RM Testing Guidelines & Safety

### Pre-Testing Preparation (Week 11)

**Reduce Volume & Intensity:**
- Week 11 (deload week) should already be lighter
- Maintain movement quality; reduce load by 20–30%
- Reduce sets by 1–2 per exercise
- Increase rest periods

**Sleep & Nutrition:**
- Prioritise 8–9 hours sleep nightly
- Maintain anti-inflammatory diet
- Increase carbs slightly (support energy for testing)
- Stay hydrated (3–4 L water daily)

**Mental Preparation:**
- Visualise successful lifts
- Review proper form cues
- Set realistic 1RM targets (based on Week 11 performance)
- Avoid excessive anxiety; testing is informational, not life-or-death

### During Testing: Form & Safety Cues

#### Trap Bar Deadlift
- **Neutral spine throughout** (no lumbar rounding or hyperextension)
- **Chest up; shoulders back**
- **Explosive drive through heels**
- **Full hip extension at top**
- **Controlled descent**
- **Stop immediately if form breaks down**

#### Dumbbell Bench Press
- **Shoulder blades retracted and depressed**
- **Elbows at 45° angle**
- **Full range of motion** (dumbbells to chest level)
- **Explosive ascent; controlled descent**
- **Stop immediately if form breaks down or pain occurs**

#### Goblet Squat
- **Chest up; neutral spine**
- **Full depth** (hips below knees, if pain-free)
- **Knees tracking over toes**
- **Explosive drive through heels**
- **Stop immediately if form breaks down**

#### Dumbbell Row
- **Neutral spine; no rotation**
- **Explosive pull; controlled descent**
- **Full retraction** (shoulder blade squeezed)
- **Elbow tucked**
- **Stop immediately if form breaks down or pain occurs**

### Red Flags: Stop Testing Immediately

- **Sharp or shooting pain** in lower back, knees, or shoulders
- **Numbness or tingling** in legs or arms
- **Loss of form** (rounding, excessive forward lean, asymmetry)
- **Feeling of instability** or "giving way"
- **Inability to complete lift** with good form (failed attempt)

### Attempt Management

**Successful Attempt:**
- Lift completed with good form
- No pain or discomfort
- Proceed to next attempt after full rest

**Failed Attempt:**
- Do NOT retry the same weight
- Rest 5 minutes
- Proceed to next attempt (if applicable)
- Maximum 5 attempts per lift

**Estimated 1RM Calculation (If Testing Stops Early):**
- Use Epley formula: 1RM = weight × (1 + reps/30)
- Example: 60 kg × 3 reps = 60 × (1 + 3/30) = 66 kg estimated 1RM

## Overview

Sleep and recovery are **non-negotiable** for your client's success. Quality sleep directly impacts:

## Sleep Foundation: The 7–9 Hour Target

### Why 7–9 Hours?

For a 42-year-old male engaged in strength training and recovery from tissue injury:
- **7 hours minimum:** Baseline for hormonal recovery and tissue repair
- **8 hours optimal:** Sweet spot for strength adaptation and cognitive function
- **9 hours:** Beneficial during high-stress training phases or injury recovery

**Research:** Studies show that sleep deprivation (< 6 hours) impairs muscle protein synthesis by up to 30%, reduces testosterone by 10–15%, and increases cortisol (pro-inflammatory).

## Sleep Hygiene Protocol

### 1. Sleep Schedule (Consistency is Key)

**Target Sleep Window:**
- **Bedtime:** 10:00–10:30 pm
- **Wake Time:** 6:00–6:30 am
- **Total Duration:** 7.5–8 hours
- **Consistency:** Same schedule 7 days per week (including weekends)

**Why Consistency Matters:**
- Regulates circadian rhythm
- Improves sleep quality and depth
- Enhances hormonal synchronisation
- Reduces sleep latency (time to fall asleep)

**Implementation:**
- Set phone alarm for bedtime (e.g., 9:45 pm reminder)
- Set wake alarm for consistent time
- Stick to schedule even on weekends (within 30 min variance acceptable)

### 2. Sleep Environment Optimisation

#### Temperature
- **Ideal bedroom temperature:** 65–68°F (18–20°C)
- **Why:** Core body temperature drops during sleep; cooler environment facilitates this
- **Action:** Use air conditioning, open windows, or adjust bedding
- **Monitor:** Use thermometer to verify; adjust as needed

#### Darkness
- **Target:** Complete darkness (< 5 lux)
- **Why:** Darkness triggers melatonin production; light suppresses it
- **Actions:**
  - Install blackout curtains or blinds
  - Remove LED lights from electronics (cover with tape)
  - Use eye mask if needed (silk, comfortable fit)
  - Avoid nightlights; use red light if bathroom trip needed

#### Sound
- **Target:** Quiet environment (< 30 dB)
- **Why:** Noise disrupts sleep architecture and REM sleep
- **Actions:**
  - Use earplugs (foam or silicone, comfortable fit)
  - White noise machine if external noise unavoidable (fan, app)
  - Soundproof curtains if traffic noise present
  - Ask household members to respect sleep time

#### Air Quality
- **Target:** Fresh, clean air; 40–60% humidity
- **Why:** Poor air quality disrupts sleep; dry air irritates airways
- **Actions:**
  - Open window 15 min before bed (if safe)
  - Use humidifier in winter (dry climates)
  - Avoid sleeping with pets (dander, movement)
  - Keep bedroom clutter-free (reduces dust)

#### Bed Quality
- **Mattress:** Supportive, comfortable, replaced every 7–10 years
- **Pillows:** Supportive, neutral neck position, replaced every 1–2 years
- **Bedding:** High-quality cotton or linen, breathable, washed weekly
- **Why:** Poor sleep surface increases pain and disrupts sleep quality

**Optimal Sleep Position for Disc Herniation Recovery:**

#### Position 1: Side-Sleeping (Preferred)
- **Setup:**
  - Lie on side (left or right, alternate nightly)
  - Pillow under head (neutral neck alignment)
  - Pillow between knees (maintains neutral spine, reduces lumbar stress)

- **Why:** Reduces spinal compression, maintains neutral alignment, reduces disc stress

#### Position 2: Supine (Back-Sleeping, Secondary)
- **Setup:**

- **Why Avoid:** Causes spinal extension and rotation; increases disc stress
- **Exception:** If client prefers, use thin pillow under abdomen to reduce lumbar extension

## Client Profile: 42M, Desk Worker, Post-Disc Herniation (L4-L5, Asymptomatic)

---

## PROGRAMME OVERVIEW

**Duration:** 12 weeks (3 phases of 4 weeks each)
**Sessions per Week:** 6 (4 strength + 2 cardio)
**Structure:** Progressive overload with strategic deloads
**Focus:** Spinal safety, strength development, anti-inflammatory recovery

### Phase Breakdown

| Phase | Weeks | Focus | Primary Goal |
|-------|-------|-------|--------------|
| **Phase 1** | 1–4 | Foundation & Stability | Movement quality, core stability, aerobic base |
| **Phase 2** | 5–8 | Strength Development | Load progression, work capacity, intensity |
| **Phase 3** | 9–12 | Strength Consolidation & Power | Maximal strength, power development, 1RM testing |

---

## WEEKLY SCHEDULE (All 12 Weeks)

| Day | Session | Duration | Focus |
|-----|---------|----------|-------|
| **Monday** | Lower Body & Core (Strength) | 50–55 min | Deadlift, core stability, glute activation |
| **Tuesday** | Upper Body Push & Pull (Strength) | 50–55 min | Bench press, rows, pulling strength |
| **Wednesday** | Cardio Session 1 | 30–40 min | Steady-state or threshold work |
| **Thursday** | Lower Body & Stability (Strength) | 50–55 min | Squat, single-leg work, stability |
| **Friday** | Upper Body & Conditioning (Strength) | 50–55 min | Rows, push-ups, conditioning finisher |
| **Saturday** | Cardio Session 2 | 30–40 min | Intervals or sport-specific conditioning |
| **Sunday** | Rest & Recovery | — | Sleep, mobility, meal prep |

## PHASE 1: FOUNDATION & STABILITY (Weeks 1–4)

### Phase 1 Goals
- Establish movement quality and neutral-spine awareness
- Build core stability and glute activation
- Assess baseline strength and movement competency
- Prepare tissues for progressive loading
- Develop aerobic base

- RPE 5–6/10 on main lifts (conversational pace)
- Focus on form over load
- Moderate volume, conservative intensity
- Deload Week 4 (reduce volume 40–50%, load 20–30%)
